answer: Persistent Work Ledger.** Each identity accrues a public history of completed jobs, paid in ember credits that decay unless renewed by activity. A new clone starts at zero and must fund its own ledger from scratch, so cloning costs the full entry fee plus the ember spent to build a usable record. Agents verify counterparties against onyx-weighted history depth before transacting, making fresh clones unemployable. Honest agents reuse one walnut-seeded keypair, letting accumulated history carry value no clone can inherit.
